info.title: Regente — integration API
info.description:
**Curated** contract of Regente's integration surface: the routes an
external system actually calls. The SPA's internal surface (Design
sessions, users, settings, alerting...) is deliberately left out — it
evolves with the UI and is not a contract.

### Authentication
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` on everything under `/api`, except where
marked public. The token is either a session issued by the UI login **or**
the deployment's static token (`REGENTE_TOKEN`, equivalent to admin — the
same one the Go SDK `pkg/client` and the `regente ops` CLI use). Auth
errors: `401` for a missing/invalid token, `403` for insufficient
role/ACL. Error bodies are `text/plain` (raw message), not JSON.

### RBAC
Reads respect the user's folder ACLs (admin sees everything). Lifecycle
actions require the `operator`/`admin` role **and** write access on the
instance's folder. Archives and export are admin-only.

### The QUERY HTTP verb
`POST /api/instances/query` also accepts the `QUERY` method (IETF httpbis
draft — safe/idempotent with a body), same handler and same contract.
OpenAPI 3.0 cannot model custom verbs, so the POST form is documented
here; `QUERY` is progressive enhancement for clients that support it.

### Ingest idempotency
`POST /api/events/ingest` is idempotent on the SENDER's key (`id` + PK in
`external_events`): an at-least-once retry answers `duplicate:true`
without reapplying any effect. Without an `id`, every POST applies (no
key, no dedupe).

servers.description: Single-origin — the server serves the API, the SPA, the docs and this contract on the same port.

tags.name: Query
tags.description: Typed composed query (D-5) and NL-query over the current day's state.

tags.name: Lifecycle
tags.description: Operational actions on an instance (classic enterprise parity) + Force Order.

tags.name: External events
tags.description: Idempotent ingestion (D-3) — another system unblocks jobs without polling.

tags.name: Daily
tags.description: State and report/SLO of the daily (E5).

tags.name: Forecast
tags.description: Simulation of what the daily would materialize (F21/CTM-6). Read-only, never touches the database.

tags.name: Catalog
tags.description: JobTypes with a declared per-type schema (ADV-1).

tags.name: Archives
tags.description: Dailies archived by the retention policy (ADV-5). Admin-only.

tags.name: Quick actions
tags.description: Single-scope HMAC links coming from alerts (D-15). The signed token IS the auth.

tags.name: Scheduler
tags.description: On-demand tick for the -scheduler=external mode (external cron).

get.description:
200 for as long as the process serves HTTP. Reports the age of the
scheduler's last tick (informational — it does NOT fail on a stale
tick: under `-scheduler=external` the tick comes from cron and failing
would cause a restart loop).

schedulerLastTickAgeSeconds.description: -1 if the scheduler has never ticked.

get.description:
"Can this node serve correct answers?" The hard gate is a reachable DB
(503 without one — point the k8s readinessProbe here). Leadership and
tick/daily age are REPORTED but never fail the check: a follower serves
the API normally.

503.description: DB unreachable — take the node out of rotation.

get.description:
Prometheus text format, no external dependency. Main gauges:
`regente_up`, `regente_env_info{env}`, `regente_instances{status}`,
`regente_agents_online`, `regente_sla_breaches_total`,
`regente_git_drift`, `regente_scheduler_last_tick_age_seconds`,
`regente_is_leader`, `regente_event_queue_depth`.

post.description:
Composed filtering beyond the query string of `/api/instances`: date
ranges, IN lists (folders/statuses), flags (forced/carried/late) and
aggregation (`groupBy`). STRICT parsing — an unknown field is a 400
(this is not SQL-over-HTTP; every filter is typed and parameterized).
An empty body `{}` means today's daily, unfiltered. Keyset pagination
via `cursor` = the id of the last item on the previous page (only
without `groupBy`).

Also accepts the `QUERY` HTTP method (same handler/contract).
post.x-permission: any logged-in user (reads filtered by folder ACLs)

200.description: Paginated list (without groupBy) OR aggregation (with groupBy).

post.description:
Interprets a natural-language question (en/pt) about the current day —
"how many jobs failed today?", "why didn't etl-sales run?" — and runs
the intent (summary/count/list/explain) against the database.
Deterministic (an intent parser, no AI). The response returns the
interpreted intent plus the structured answer.
post.x-permission: any logged-in user (reads filtered by folder ACLs)

answer.description: Structured answer (its shape varies with the kind — text/count/byStatus/items...).

get.summary: Detail of one instance (+ the order's frozen action)
get.description:
The full runtime row plus what the list deliberately does NOT carry
(scale payload): `label`, `jobType` and `actionConfig` extracted from
the `definition_snapshot` — the photo of the definition frozen when the
instance was ordered, the SAME one the dispatch executes. Editing the
job in Design after the order does not change this response. A folder
the user cannot read answers 404 (it does not leak existence).
get.x-permission: any logged-in user (reads filtered by folder ACLs)

404.description: Instance not found (or folder not readable).

delete.summary: Delete — removes the order (ONLY on HOLD)
delete.description:
The classic "Delete job": removes the instance from the screen and from
the state store. Requires the job to be on HOLD — since RUNNING is not
holdable, a job in execution is never deletable; any other status
becomes deletable by going through Hold first. The dependency-event
ledger stays intact: an OK consumption that was held remains spent (the
rerun of a clone stays in WAIT EVENT); an unconsumed reservation goes
back to the pool.
delete.x-permission: operator/admin + write access on the instance's folder

409.description: Not on HOLD (hold it first; RUNNING is not deletable).

post.summary: Hold — holds an instance (any status except RUNNING)
post.description:
General hold: any status → HELD, except RUNNING (409 — the execution is
already on the agent; cancel it or wait) and HELD itself (an idempotent
no-op that echoes the current state). The original status is frozen in
`heldFromStatus` and Release restores THAT — holding an OK and
releasing it re-executes nothing.
post.x-permission: operator/admin + write access on the instance's folder

200.description: Hold applied (or a no-op if it was already HELD).

post.description:
HELD → the ORIGINAL status frozen by the hold (`heldFromStatus`; legacy
holds without it fall back to WAITING). A released WAITING re-enters
normal gating on the next tick; a released OK/NOTOK simply goes back to
being OK/NOTOK. A job held by a FOLDER PAUSE answers 409 — only the
folder resume releases it.
post.x-permission: operator/admin + write access on the instance's folder

200.description: Release applied (or a no-op if it was not HELD).

409.description: Held by a folder pause (release it through the folder).

post.description: Marks it CANCELLED (unconditionally) and closes finished_at.
post.x-permission: operator/admin + write access on the instance's folder

post.description:
Clears started/finished/exitCode/output and goes back to WAITING. The
`confirmed` flag SURVIVES the rerun (BUG-2): an already-confirmed job
does not fall back to the CONFIRM gate. Pending alerts for the job are
marked as handled; the tick is nudged — with the gates satisfied, the
job goes in right away.
post.x-permission: operator/admin + write access on the instance's folder

post.description:
The classic "Set OK": marks it OK, publishes the dependency event and
MATERIALIZES the ConditionsOut — unblocking the on-success successors.
It also applies to WAITING (a job stuck on WAIT EVENT finishes OK right
away, BUG-3). 400 if the instance is not in an eligible state (e.g.
RUNNING).
post.x-permission: operator/admin + write access on the instance's folder

post.description:
The classic "Confirm": releases a job defined with `confirm: true`. It
applies to WAITING and HELD (confirming while held counts; it runs once
released). Not even Force bypasses this gate — only Confirm. It nudges
the tick: confirmed, dispatched.
post.x-permission: operator/admin + write access on the instance's folder

400.description: Instance not found, or not on WAITING/HELD.

post.summary: Force Order — materializes the published def into today's daily
post.description:
The classic "Order Force": creates an instance from the most current
PUBLISHED definition, right now, in today's daily (the regular daily is
an immutable photo; force picks up the live def — only for the forced
job).
post.x-permission: operator/admin + write access on the definition's folder

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The definition ID (the YAML id in the workspace).

post.summary: Idempotent ingestion of an external event (D-3)
post.description:
Another system (CDC, pipeline, vendor webhook) reports that something
happened — and that unblocks jobs WITHOUT polling: it sets conditions
(scoped by `date`, defaulting to today in the business timezone) and/or
forces a job.

**Idempotent** on the sender's key: `id` is the PK — an at-least-once
retry answers `duplicate: true` without reapplying. **Persisted**: the
event and what it caused (`applied`) stay in the table (forensics for
"who unblocked this job at 03:14"). **Immediate**: it nudges the tick.

Requires `conditions[]` (or `condition`) and/or `forceJob` — nothing to
apply is a 400.

200.description:
Event accepted. `duplicate: false` + `applied` (the list of what was
done, item by item, with partial ERRORs inline) — or
`duplicate: true` + `applied: false` on a retry (nothing reapplied).

get.description:
Last materialization + the configured time (`settings.daily_at`) + the
business timezone (E1). `orderDate`/`serverNow` are in the business
timezone — that is the clock that decides what "today" means.

The summary operations asks for at the end of the day: counts per
state, punctuality of the materialization (`lateStart`, 5-minute
tolerance), whether the day "closed" (`closed` — nothing
WAITING/RUNNING), failures (capped at 100, the count is always exact)
and SLA breaches. It is also the payload of the optional push
(`daily_report_channels`).

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: YYYY-MM-DD; defaults to today's daily in the business timezone.

get.description:
Simulates in RAM what the daily would materialize on `date`: who is
eligible (the SAME gating as RunDaily — frequency, include/exclude
calendars, shift, via IsScheduledOn), topological order (waves), blocks
from deps/resources/conditions and projected SLA violations. It never
touches the database.
One ForecastReport per day, same gating as RunDaily. The classic "≥1 week".

The DEDICATED schema of every jobType (fields, required ones, kinds,
enums, aliases), straight from the registry the validator uses — the
same source as the DRAFT-on-save / STRICT-on-publish validation. The
documentation baseline for integrators and payload generation.

items.description: Schema per type (name/label/fields...) — driven by the server.

get.description:
The NDJSON files the post-daily retention GC writes into
`settings.archive_dir`. Admin-only (an archive carries output and
snapshots from ALL folders — it does not go through per-team RBAC).

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The exact name in the instances-YYYY-MM-DD[-N].ndjson format (anything else is a 400).

post.description:
Fires one scheduling cycle (materializes the daily if it is due +
dispatch). Designed for `-scheduler=external`, where an external cron
(Cloud Scheduler, k8s CronJob, GitHub Actions) hits this instead of the
internal ticker. Idempotent and leader-guarded — safe to call
frequently. In serverless, a per-tick lock serializes overlapping ticks
across containers (ARCH-3).

Materializes today's daily IF the configured time has passed and it has
not run yet (idempotent, leader-guarded), **without** running the
dispatch cycle. Designed to split the cadences in serverless: a
minute-level cron on `/scheduler/tick` (dispatch) and a **daily** cron
here (materialization) — instead of every tick checking the daily.

get.description:
A signed link (HMAC, 24h TTL, single instance+action scope) that
arrives with the alert. GET NEVER executes — a link preview in a chat
must not trigger a rerun; the page shows the button that does the POST.
No Authorization header: the signed token itself is the auth.

post.description:
Verifies the token and EXECUTES the embedded action (same semantics as
the lifecycle handlers; actor = "quick-action"). The response is
feedback HTML.

409.description: Action not applied — the instance's state does not allow it (HTML).

bearerAuth.description: A login session OR the deployment's static token (REGENTE_TOKEN = admin).

instanceId.name: id
instanceId.description: The instance ID (e.g. the `id` returned by the composed query).

qaToken.name: token
qaToken.description: Signed HMAC token (issued by alerting; 24h TTL).

Forbidden.description: Insufficient role/ACL (writer, admin or write access on the folder).

Instance.description:
One instance in the daily (an IMMUTABLE snapshot of the order —
team/dryRun and friends freeze at the moment the job is ordered).

carriedFrom.description: The day of origin if it came from another daily's carry-over.

confirmed.description: Confirm gate opened (jobs with confirm: true).

cycleRuns.description: OK laps completed during the day (cyclic jobs).

dryRun.description: Frozen on the order (the GHOST badge).

allOf.description: Fields extracted from definition_snapshot (the photo of the order).

label.description: The job label frozen on the order.

jobType.description: The job type (COMMAND/SCRIPT/...) frozen on the order.

actionConfig.description: Action parameters (e.g. command/cwd) frozen on the order — what the dispatch executes.

StructuredQuery.description: Everything optional; the zero value means today's daily, unfiltered. An unknown field is a 400.

forced.description: Only forced ones (true) / only non-forced ones (false).

carried.description: Only carry-overs from another daily (true) / only native ones (false).

late.description: true = WAITING with scheduledAt in the past (late).

groupBy.description: Aggregation in the database — switches the response to the grouped shape.

cursor.description: Keyset — the id of the last item on the previous page.

nextCursor.description: Pass it back in `cursor` for the next page; empty means there is nothing left.

QueryResultGrouped.description: The aggregated shape (with groupBy) — counters straight from the database, no row materialized.

id.description: The SENDER's dedupe key (PK). Omitted means no dedupe — every POST applies.

kind.description: A free-form label for the event type (file-arrived, job-done...).

forceJob.description: The definition to force into the daily.

date.description: Scope of the conditions; defaults to today (business tz).

applied.description:
The list of what was applied (with partial ERRORs inline) — or the
boolean `false` when it is a duplicate (nothing reapplied).
A "; "-separated summary of what the event caused.

timezone.description: IANA (settings.daily_timezone); empty means the server's local clock.

lateStart.description: Materialized >5 min after the configured time (the scheduler's punctuality SLO).

closed.description: Nothing WAITING/RUNNING — the day closed (the push trigger).

failures.description: Capped at 100 items; counts.notok is always exact.

reportSent.description: The daily push was already sent (report_sent_at).

reason.description: Why it does not run ("no calendar match", "blocked by deps"...).

schedulerStale.description: Last tick more than 120s ago (informational, does not fail).
